doc.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Recordings as a leader and the Getz years
title: Peruvian Blue and his use of percussion
summary: Barron explains his taste for Latin percussion from Symphony Sid's Latin shows.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: I’m going to go back down through your discography as a leader. Then, the next one, 1974, on Muse again, Peruvian Blue. You’re bringing in your colleague Ted Dunbar, Dave Williams, Tootie Heath, Richard Landrum, and then Sonny Morgan. You always had a percussionist in there. You like – is that from Diz? Is that a Diz influence? What’s going on?

I don’t know. I just like Latin stuff. It was when I first came – I didn’t hear a lot of it in Philly, but when I came to New York, I used to listen to Symphony Sid, and he had a Latin show. So I got to hear a lot of salsa and stuff. I really grew to love it. So, whenever I did a record, I always thought about using percussion. Sonny – Sonny Morgan – I don’t know what ever happened. I think he was from Philly too.
